content.text:
I tidied up `0.html` without changing how it looks on a normal desktop screen: it is still a 400px black circle centred on the page. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

## What changed

- **No stray horizontal scrollbar:** removed `width: 100vw` from `body`, which overflows whenever a vertical scrollbar is present.
- **Better mobile height:** `height: 100vh` became `min-height: 100dvh`, with `100vh` kept as a fallback, so the circle stays centred when mobile browser toolbars show or hide.
- **Scales on small screens:** the SVG is now `width: min(400px, 100vmin)` instead of a fixed 400px, so it shrinks rather than being clipped on narrow viewports.
- **Accessible:** the SVG has `role="img"` and a `<title>` ("Black circle") so screen readers announce it.
- **Small CSS cleanup:** added `box-sizing: border-box` to the reset, switched centring to `grid` with `place-items: center`, and set the SVG to `display: block`.

## What I left alone

- **Page title and id:** `ae683f770` looks generated, so I kept it. A descriptive `<title>` would be better if this page is meant for people to see.
- **Dark mode:** the circle is still hard-coded black on the default white background. Adding `color-scheme: light dark` with `fill: currentColor` would make it adapt, but that changes the look, so I didn't do it.
